title: Festive Capsule Wardrobe: 5 Indian Outfits for Dec to Feb
excerpt: A five-outfit Indian capsule wardrobe for December to February that covers Christmas, New Year's Eve, winter weddings and Valentine's Day.
body:
A festive capsule wardrobe for December to February needs just five Indian outfits: one statement Anarkali, one sparkly suit, two versatile kurta sets and one embroidered kurti. Mix and match the dupattas, jewellery and layers, and these five pieces will carry you through Christmas, New Year's Eve, winter weddings and Valentine's Day without a last-minute panic.

*By the Bahe Kurtiz styling team, Jaipur. Each piece is stitched in our own Jaipur unit, with block prints printed by hand by karigars.*

**Quick answer**

- Outfit 1: a taffeta Anarkali for weddings and big parties
- Outfit 2: a sequin embroidered suit for New Year's Eve and sangeets
- Outfit 3: an embroidered kota doria kurta set for church, puja and day functions
- Outfit 4: a block print kurta set for lunches and casual festive days
- Outfit 5: an embroidered kurti for office parties and dates
- Swap dupattas between sets to create new looks

## Why build a festive capsule wardrobe?

The three months from December to February are the busiest of the year for many Indian families abroad. You have Christmas on 25 December, New Year's Eve on 31 December, the Indian wedding season (roughly November to February), and Valentine's Day on 14 February. Buying a new outfit for every event is expensive and leaves your wardrobe full of pieces worn once.

A capsule wardrobe solves this. You choose a small set of outfits that work together, then restyle them for each occasion. It saves money, packing space and decision time.

## Which five outfits should be in the capsule?

### Outfit 1: The statement Anarkali

This is your hero piece for weddings, receptions and big parties. The [lavender taffeta silk Anarkali with organza dupatta](/products/lavender-taffeta-silk-gota-work-anarkali-suit-set-with-organza-dupatta/) is a great choice. Lavender is soft enough for a day wedding yet rich enough for an evening, and gota work adds a festive glow.

### Outfit 2: The sparkly suit

For New Year's Eve and sangeet nights, you want shine and movement. The [violet Nyra cut sequin embroidered cotton suit](/products/violet-nyra-cut-sequin-embroidered-cotton-3-piece-suit/) has sequins that catch the light, and cotton keeps it comfortable for dancing.

### Outfit 3: The elegant kurta set

You need one polished kurta set for church, puja, day functions and lunch with elders. The [navy blue kota doria embroidered kurta set](/products/navy-blue-kota-doria-embroidered-kurta-pant-dupatta-set/) is calm, classic and works with gold or silver jewellery.

### Outfit 4: The easy block print set

This is your everyday festive outfit for family lunches, gift-shopping and quieter days. The [indigo hand block print kota doria kurta set with printed cotton pants](/products/indigo-hand-block-print-kota-doria-kurta-pant-dupatta-set/) is printed by hand, light to layer, and easy to dress up or down.

### Outfit 5: The embroidered kurti

For office parties, dates and Christmas Eve, a kurti over jeans or trousers is perfect. The [bottle green embroidered kurti with side tie-up](/products/green-embroidered-kurti/) brings in a seasonal green and goes with most of your existing wardrobe.

## How do the five outfits cover every event?

| Outfit | Christmas | New Year's Eve | Winter wedding | Valentine's Day |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lavender taffeta Anarkali | Christmas dinner | Gala dinner | Reception, sangeet | Formal dinner |
| Violet sequin suit | Christmas party | House party | Sangeet, mehendi | Party night |
| Navy kota doria set | Church service | Daytime plans | Puja, pheras | Lunch with family |
| Indigo block print set | Family lunch | Day of rest | Haldi, day events | Brunch |
| Bottle green kurti | Christmas Eve | Casual drinks | Welcome dinner | Dinner date |

## How do I restyle the same outfits?

Restyling is where a capsule really earns its place. Three simple tricks change the look completely.

- **Swap the dupatta:** wear the lavender organza dupatta with the navy set for a softer evening look
- **Change the jewellery:** gold jhumkas feel traditional, silver hoops feel modern
- **Change the hair:** a sleek bun for evenings, loose waves or a braid for day events

You can also wear the bottle green kurti with the indigo set's printed pants for a new Indo-western mix. Our guide on how to [restyle one Anarkali for three functions](/blog/one-anarkali-three-wedding-functions-restyle-guide/) has many more ideas.

> **From our Jaipur studio:** When we plan a festive season, we think in colour families. Lavender, violet, navy and indigo all sit in the cool family, so dupattas and jewellery move easily between them. Bottle green adds a single contrast that works with every one.

## What should I add for cold weather?

A capsule is not complete without layers. Add one long coat in a neutral like camel or black, one wool or pashmina shawl, thin thermal leggings and a fitted thermal top. With these four pieces, all five outfits work in a UK, Canadian or northern US winter. For Australia, where December to February is summer, you can skip most of the layers.

If you are attending a full wedding, see our guide on how to [plan your wardrobe for a 5-function Indian wedding](/blog/how-to-plan-your-wardrobe-for-a-5-function-indian-wedding/).

## When should I order my capsule?

Order early, especially if you want everything custom fitted. Made-to-measure pieces take 5–7 working days to make, plus about 5–10 business days for delivery, so order at least 3–4 weeks before your first event. Ready sizes ship in 2–4 working days. Shipping to the USA, UK, Canada, UAE and Australia is free and duties-paid. See all our [wedding guest outfits](/indian-wedding-guest-outfits/) for more options.

## Our pick for you

If you can only buy two pieces now, start with the lavender Anarkali and the navy kota doria set, then add the others as your calendar fills up. A small etiquette note: when rewearing the same outfit at events with the same guests, change the dupatta and jewellery so it feels fresh.

## Frequently asked questions

**How many Indian outfits do I need for the festive season?**
Five well-chosen outfits can cover Christmas, New Year's Eve, a winter wedding and Valentine's Day if you restyle them with dupattas, jewellery and layers.

**Is it okay to repeat an outfit at Indian functions?**
Yes. Many women repeat outfits across different events. Change the dupatta, jewellery and hair to give it a new look.

**What colours work best for a festive capsule wardrobe?**
Choose colours from one family, like cool lavenders, blues and violets, and add one contrast shade, like bottle green, so pieces mix easily.

**How do I keep my festive outfits fresh between events?**
Air them out after wearing, steam rather than iron heavy pieces, and store them folded in cotton bags away from damp.
